quotes.quote: Voicebox: Text-Guided Multilingual Universal Speech Generation at Scale
This paper presents Voicebox, the most versatile generative model for speech.
Infilling can be considered as another type of task. It aims to predict speech content
Transient noise removal & content editing
Content editing and speech denoising can be productivity tools for users to create content more effortlessly.
Zero-shot TTS & alignment-preserved style transfer
Cross-lingual:
cross-lingual zero-shot TTS results, where the audio context and the target text are in different languages.
We create a test set for each language by selecting samples from the MLS test split
The speaker similarity consistently improves as the prompt length is increased
Table D12: Detailed configurations for conditional flow matching based duration models
we also present a few standalone metrics focusing on the duration model.
Our first metric, multi-sample mean-absolute error (MS-MAE)
Measuring speech diversity and quality with FSD
We adapt the metric for speech by using self-supervised wav2vec 2.0 features
Both Voicebox variants beat the baseline by a large margin.
Prior studies often adopt subjective metrics like mean opinion scores (MOS)
Voicebox depends on a phonemizer and a forced aligner to produce frame-level phonetic transcript.
Voicebox models presented in this paper are trained on read speech from audiobooks in up to six written languages.
a small amount of utterances were excluded due to MFA alignment failure.

decisions.answer:
R1: unknown. No evidence about click/pop artifacts at edit boundaries.
R2: Yes, 3-second clips are used as prompts for zero-shot TTS and cross-lingual transfer.
R3: Yes, supports cross-lingual zero-shot TTS so an English speaker can speak other languages in their own voice.
R4: Yes, denoising is an intended application, but detailed denoising quality is not quantified here.
R5: unknown. No direct evidence on emotional expressiveness vs robotic sound.
R6: unknown. No mention of code or pretrained weights availability.
decisions.notes:
R1: Only high-level 'content editing' and 'transient noise removal' are mentioned, not artifact-free splicing. [bfc84f074f6f7130][12c19f9c07484725]
R2: Cross-lingual experiments explicitly use 'one 3-second long audio context' as prompts. [3c30f4acf734928f]
R3: Paper discusses cross-lingual zero-shot TTS where audio context and target text are different languages, and applications where 'everyone' can speak any language in their own voice. [3c30f4acf734928f][12c19f9c07484725][ff1b257a1da60f08]
R4: Speech denoising is listed as an application: 'speech denoising can be productivity tools'. No quantitative denoising metrics in provided chunks. [12c19f9c07484725]
R5: Chunks discuss diversity, WER, and metrics, but not subjective emotion/expressiveness, so this remains unknown.
R6: No chunk mentions code release or pretrained weights; only describes the model and experiments, so availability is unknown.
